current.text: He is a first-round rookie point guard drafted by OKC.
He is behind Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Nikola Topic in the guard rotation. OKC also has to find more minutes for Jared McCain.
Expected to get some volume, but he is a long way from fantasy relevance.
His Summer League was fine but not great: 14 points and 3 assists in 28 minutes, shooting 30% from three.
Josh dropped him from tier five to tier six in his dynasty rookie ranks. He still does not like the pick.
OKC traded away Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, its main shooters, and the rotation is still deep.
OKC could be one of the lowest-volume three-point teams unless players like Stirtz shoot more. That leaves a small opening for him as a shooter.

durable.text: He is an older, undersized guard.
He runs the pick and roll well.
He was not asked to shoot much in college.
He projects as a great three-point shooter off the ball.

note: Stirtz is not a draft option for our 144-player auction. Yahoo values him at 0 USD and ranks him 686th, and his projection of 5.4 points and 1.6 rebounds in a small role gives almost nothing outside low turnovers. He goes straight to waivers. Watch him early only if an injury among OKC guards gives him minutes, or if the team starts using him as a high-volume three-point shooter to replace the shooting it lost.
